classification.difficultyReason: Match vertices from supplied angles and side markings, then translate those correspondences into ordered triangle names despite changes in orientation.

content.prompt: Write a congruence statement for each pair of congruent triangles.

spec.description: Horizontal pair of right triangles with corresponding angle symbols, right-angle squares and side ticks. Ordinary source blue outlines use house black.
spec.mathematics: A corresponds to X, B to Z and C to Y; AC and XY have one tick; AB and XZ have two ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied markings remain visible; no congruence statement is supplied.

answer.worked: $A\leftrightarrow X$ are right-angle vertices, $B\leftrightarrow Z$ have angle $\alpha$, and $C\leftrightarrow Y$ have angle $\beta$. Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle XZY$.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
$\triangle ABC$ is isosceles with $CA=CB$.

$\triangle DEF$ is isosceles with $FD=FE$.

spec.description: Paired upright isosceles triangles; both equal legs carry one tick and both bases carry two ticks. Source captions remain editable in the prompt. Ordinary outlines use black.
spec.mathematics: A and B have angle alpha; C has beta. D and E have alpha; F has beta. Either order of the second triangle's base vertices gives a valid correspondence.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied angle and equality markings only.

answer.worked: The apex correspondence is $C\leftrightarrow F$. The equal base angles allow either $A\leftrightarrow D$, $B\leftrightarrow E$, or $A\leftrightarrow E$, $B\leftrightarrow D$. Thus $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle DEF$ or $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle EDF$.

spec.description: Horizontal pair of identically oriented oblique triangles; retain one-, two- and three-tick correspondences and all three Greek angle labels. Ordinary outlines use black.
spec.mathematics: A corresponds to E, B to F, C to G; AC and EG have one tick, AB and EF two, BC and FG three.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens visible, answer statement absent.

answer.worked: The matching angles and side ticks give $A\leftrightarrow E$, $B\leftrightarrow F$ and $C\leftrightarrow G$. Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle EFG$.

spec.description: Differently oriented triangles, MNO above-left and XYZ below-right; preserve the spatial comparison, internal angle values and external 10 cm labels. Ordinary outlines use black.
spec.mathematics: M and X have 20 degrees, N and Y have 130 degrees, NO and YZ are 10 cm; O corresponds to Z.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied two angles and side length in each triangle are visible.

answer.worked: The equal angles give $M\leftrightarrow X$ and $N\leftrightarrow Y$; the corresponding $10\text{ cm}$ sides give $O\leftrightarrow Z$. Therefore $\triangle MNO\equiv\triangle XYZ$.
